title: Impossibility of One-Way One-Round Quantum 4-Coloring via Matrix-Space Stability
abstract: We show that one-way one-round quantum LOCAL algorithms cannot $4$-color directed cycles with high probability, even with unbounded local computation and quantum message length. This is the first lower bound in the high-probability quantum LOCAL setting that goes beyond the non-signaling and bounded-dependence models, exploiting the structure of distributed quantum algorithms.   Our proof connects distributed quantum computing with noncommutative extremal combinatorics by identifying local collision probabilities with the weighted multiplicative energy of matrix-space decompositions. We obtain our lower bound by proving a dimension-independent weighted stability theorem for a directed noncommutative analogue of Mantel's theorem.
summary: This work establishes a fundamental impossibility result for quantum computation, proving that no one-way one-round quantum algorithm can reliably 4-color directed cycles. The authors achieve this by developing a deep connection between quantum graph coloring and noncommutative extremal combinatorics, using matrix energy bounds to derive the necessary lower bound.
main_problem: The paper proves a quantum lower bound demonstrating that a one-way one-round quantum LOCAL algorithm cannot 4-color directed cycles with high probability.
main_result: The impossibility of such a quantum coloring is established by connecting the problem to a lower bound on the $\Lambda$-energy of matrix-space decompositions.
method: The proof employs noncommutative extremal combinatorics, mapping the quantum coloring problem to bounding the $\Lambda$-energy of a set of POVM elements.
model_or_system: The model is the quantum LOCAL algorithm applied to graph coloring, specifically directed cycles. The analysis uses quantum information tools like POVMs and matrix energy bounds.
important_parameters: The number of colors ($q=4$), the locality (one-way, one-round), and the size of the local random-seed space ($N$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the quantum coloring problem can be mapped to the energy bound, and the lower bound is shown to be stronger than those from bounded-dependence models.
paper_structure: The paper develops the argument by first establishing classical lower bounds, then generalizing this to the quantum setting using matrix energy bounds, culminating in the proof that the energy lower bound implies the coloring impossibility.
why_interesting: It provides a strong, non-trivial lower bound for quantum computation models, showing limitations beyond classical or simpler quantum models, which is fundamental for understanding quantum algorithm complexity.
